Welcome to WNBA & NBA Statistical Leaders! 🏀

    💡 How to Use the Interactive Visualizations
    
      Filter Categories: On the Graphs tab, use the dropdown menu to toggle between Points, Rebounds, Blocks, Assists, Steals, and Personal Fouls.
      Hover for Details: Hover over any individual data point to view the player name, team, game date, minutes, and exact statistics.
      Zoom & Pan: Click and drag across clusters of points to zoom in; double-click to reset the axes.
      Trendlines: Dashed regression lines show the linear relationship fitted across the full dataset of 12,013 games.

title: 📋 Project Overview
text:
🏀 The Mission
        
          This project explores the relationship between playing time (minutes) and statistical output across both the 
          WNBA and NBA for the 2025–2026 seasons.
        
      
    
  

  
    
      
        📊 Key Categories
        Six vital box score indicators examined across every game:
        
          🏀 Points
          🔄 Rebounds
          🤝 Assists
          ⚡ Steals
          🛡️ Blocks
          ⚠️ Personal Fouls
        
      
    
  

  
    
      
        📦 Data & Methodology
        
          WNBA Source: SportsDataverse (wehoop)
          NBA Source: ESPN via SportsDataverse (hoopR)
          Sample & Modeling: 2,000 sampled individual performances with linear regression trendlines fitted across 12,013 total games per league.

        📦 About the Data
        
          The datasets comprise 12,013 individual player-game box scores from the 2025–2026 regular seasons:
        
        
          WNBA Data: Sourced via SportsDataverse (wehoop).
          NBA Data: Sourced from ESPN via SportsDataverse (hoopR).
        
        
          
            To ensure a balanced comparison across both leagues, each league's sample contains 12,013 observations, with 2,000 performances plotted in each interactive visualization. The dashed trendlines represent linear regressions fitted across all 12,013 games.

title: ⭐ Story
text:
🏀
      
        Meet the Creator
        Shania Leubin · New College of Florida
      
    
    
    
      My name is Shania Leubin. I graduated from Lemon Bay High School and now attend the New College of Florida. My area of concentration is Finance, while also studying pre-law!
    

    

    Why I Chose This Project?! 🎯
    
    
      As a basketball player and fan, I became interested in analyzing Women’s Basketball statistics. After comparing players across multiple seasons and researching reliable data sources, I discovered a positive correlation between minutes played and points, assists, steals, rebounds, and blocks.
    
    
    
      
        "This inspired me to create a website using graphs and data to highlight player performance, celebrate their legacies, and showcase the growth of Women’s Basketball. I have also compared my data to Men's Basketball to prove that women are just as capable as men."

This project explores the relationship between playing time (minutes) and statistical output across both the WNBA and NBA for the 2025–2026 seasons.

Data Sources:

WNBA: SportsDataverse (wehoop)
NBA: ESPN (hoopR)

Key Categories: Points, Rebounds, Assists, Steals, Blocks, and Personal Fouls.
Sample: Both leagues display 2,000 sampled individual game performances with linear regression trendlines calculated across all 12,013 games.



My name is Shania Leubin. I graduated from Lemon Bay High School and now attend the New College of Florida. My area of concentration is Finance, while also studying pre-law!

Why I chose this project?!
As a basketball player and fan, I became interested in analyzing Women’s Basketball statistics. After comparing players across multiple seasons and researching reliable data sources, I discovered a positive correlation between minutes played and points, assists, steals, rebounds, and blocks. This inspired me to create a website using graphs and data to highlight player performance, celebrate their legacies, and showcase the growth of Women’s Basketball. I have also compared my data to Men’s Basketball to prove that women are just as capable as men.

To ensure a balanced comparison across both leagues, each league’s sample contains 12,013 observations, with 2,000 performances plotted in each interactive visualization. The dashed trendlines represent linear regressions fitted across all 12,013 games.
